top_articles.title: Credo (CRDO) vs. Marvell (MRVL): Which AI Chip Stock Is the Better Buy?
top_articles.summary: Credo Technology and Marvell Technology are compared as AI chip investment options. Credo offers faster near-term growth (87% revenue growth projected for FY2027) with better valuation at 30X forward earnings, but faces concentration risk with 4 customers representing 84% of revenue. Marvell provides broader AI infrastructure exposure with stronger long-term earnings growth but trades at a premium 72X multiple. Both stocks receive a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

top_articles.title: Buy TI and NVIDIA for Exposure to Semiconductor Boom
top_articles.summary: The semiconductor industry is positioned for exceptional growth through 2026-2027, driven primarily by AI infrastructure demand and data-center expansion. Global semiconductor sales are expected to grow 89.9% in 2026 to $1.51 trillion, with memory and AI infrastructure as primary drivers. However, near-term challenges include geopolitical tensions, supply-chain constraints, elevated memory prices, and potential tariff impacts. NVIDIA and Texas Instruments are highlighted as top picks to benefit from this cycle.

top_articles.title: 3 AI Stocks Poised to Outperform Micron and Sandisk as the Next Infrastructure Bottleneck Builds
top_articles.summary: As AI infrastructure demands evolve beyond chips and memory, three companies are positioned to capitalize on emerging bottlenecks: Innodata provides data organization services with 58% revenue growth; Nebius offers neocloud services with expanding data center capacity and rising per-megawatt contract values; and Vertiv supplies critical liquid cooling solutions for AI infrastructure with 24% revenue growth and accelerating demand.

top_articles.title: The AI Company You Haven't Heard of -- But Should Keep on Your Radar
top_articles.summary: Bloom Energy, a fuel-cell technology company founded in 2001, is positioned to benefit significantly from AI infrastructure expansion. The company helps data centers obtain electricity faster by generating power on-site, addressing grid capacity constraints. After years of losses, Bloom Energy achieved profitability in early 2026 with 166% revenue growth in Q2, driven by major enterprise customers like Oracle. As data center power consumption is projected to reach 12% of U.S. electricity by 2030, Bloom Energy could become a standard supplier in the rapidly expanding data-center ecosystem.

top_articles.title: Chip Stocks Recovered Today and the Major Indexes Fell Anyway

top_articles.title: Is WisdomTree U.S. Multifactor ETF (USMF) a Strong ETF Right Now?

Year-to-date returns are 2.8%, though cheaper alternatives like ITOT and VTI with lower expense ratios (0.03%) may be more suitable for cost-conscious investors.

top_articles.title: Should You Invest in the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM)?
top_articles.summary: The iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM) is a passively managed fund with $10.63 billion in assets, offering broad exposure to the technology sector with a low 0.37% expense ratio. The fund has gained 24.33% year-to-date and 31.31% over the past year, with top holdings including Microsoft (9.9%), Nvidia, and Apple. IGM carries a beta of 1.40 and holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 1 (Strong Buy), though alternatives like XLK and VGT offer lower expense ratios.

top_articles.title: If I Were in My 20s, I'd Buy This Unstoppable Vanguard ETF and Hold It Forever
top_articles.summary: The article recommends the Vanguard S&P 500 Growth ETF (VOOG) for young investors in their 20s as a long-term buy-and-hold investment. The ETF focuses on 148 growth stocks from the S&P 500, with over 51% in technology companies. It has delivered 16.9% compound annual returns since 2010, outpacing the S&P 500's 14.2%, and could potentially double retirement savings over 40 years due to compounding.

top_articles.title: Where Tesla's Robotaxi Rollout Stands Today and What Investors Should Know
top_articles.summary: Tesla launched its Cybercab robotaxi service in Austin on September 3, showcasing improvements in manufacturing efficiency with a 50% reduction in production line size and highlighting that vehicles require no rare-earth minerals. However, the event was less impressive than anticipated, with CEO Elon Musk absent and the stock pulling back following the announcement. The launch was also accompanied by NHTSA safety and regulatory compliance reviews, raising questions about the timeline for autonomous vehicle commercialization. With Tesla's EV business plateauing and Optimus robots years away from revenue generation, the Cybercab's success is critical to the company's growth narrative.

top_articles.title: Elon Musk's $1 Trillion Pay Package Needs Tesla to Hit an $8.5 Trillion Market Cap. Here's What That Means for Shareholders.
top_articles.summary: Tesla shareholders approved a $1 trillion pay package for CEO Elon Musk in November, contingent on meeting 12 performance milestones over 10 years. The package requires Tesla to reach an $8.5 trillion market cap and achieve significant operational goals in robotics, FSD subscriptions, and robotaxis. While the best-case scenario of all milestones being met appears unlikely, even partial completion would significantly benefit shareholders and diversify Tesla's revenue streams beyond traditional auto sales.

Instead, investors should consider Nvidia (which supplies chips to all robotics companies), Alphabet (with Google Cloud and Waymo autonomous vehicles), and Zebra Technologies (providing foundational software for robots), all trading at more attractive valuations with more certain growth catalysts.
